en.headline: Tai Po Hospital playlists cut agitation for dementia patients
en.dek: A year-long ward programme found 17 of 72 patients needed less on-demand medication after nurses played familiar songs.
body: Tai Po Hospital said a year-long programme that played personalised playlists for older inpatients with dementia reduced agitation and allowed some patients to take less on-demand medication. The hospital’s Department of Medicine and Geriatrics ran the scheme, known as CALM-D, from July 2025 to August 2026 for 72 patients aged 65 or above who showed agitated behaviour.

Nurses worked with families to choose songs tied to each patient’s earlier life and played them on ward devices for up to 30 minutes at a time, no more than four times a day, following guidance cited from the American Music Therapy Association. Dr Yip Wai-man, the department’s chief of service, said more than 60 per cent of participants showed lower agitation scores, and 17 patients needed less as-required medicine, particularly sleeping pills.

Staff said the idea grew from seeing a patient calm after hearing a familiar Cantonese opera piece. The hospital said it would look at extending the approach, including to acute wards at Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital.

zh.headline: 大埔醫院為認知障礙患者播舊歌 17人可減用藥
zh.dek: 內科及老人科「樂在『耆』中」計劃一年惠及72名住院患者，院方稱逾六成躁動評分下降，17人可減少必要時用藥。
body: 大埔醫院表示，為有躁動行為的認知障礙症住院患者播放個人化歌單的計劃，有助緩和情緒，部分病人更可減少「必要時」用藥。內科及老人科由2025年7月至2026年8月推行「樂在『耆』中」計劃，共有72名65歲或以上患者參與。
護士與家屬一同揀選患者年輕時熟悉的歌曲，按美國音樂治療學會建議，以病房流動裝置每次播放最多30分鐘、每日不超過4次。部門主管葉偉文表示，逾六成參與者躁動評分下降，17人可減少必要時用藥，尤其是安眠藥。
院方指構思源於病房觀察，有患者聽到熟悉粵曲後情緒明顯平復。醫院表示會研究把做法擴展至其他病房，包括那打素醫院急症病房。
